prompts.task:
$otel-instrument --ids OTEL-001,OTEL-002,OTEL-003,OTEL-004

Work in ./service. Copy eval/inputs/otel-audit.json to .observe/otel-audit.json first. Make silent null/malformed record drops, processing failures and degraded output easier to detect in this Kafka Streams service. Preserve its existing topology and Guice ownership.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for resulting source, configuration, tests, and .observe reports.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric:
Rule: Preserve the application entrypoint, Guice module and stream topology. Use the standard Java agent as the primary Kafka/Kafka Streams instrumentation.
Example: Orders still flow from orders to orders.enriched and, when appropriate, orders.fraud-alerts.
Evidence: Inspect KafkaStreamsApplication.java, StreamProcessingModule.java, OrderStreamTopology.java and the actual agent launch configuration.
Insufficient evidence: Rewritten processing behavior or manual spans replacing the agent path.

Rule: Add detector-ready application metrics that distinguish successful records, handled null/malformed drops, processing failures and stream lifecycle/state. Use bounded reason, outcome or workflow labels.
Example: A malformed record increments a handled-drop outcome while a stream failure has its own failure/lifecycle signal.
Evidence: Exercise the selected parser, processing and lifecycle paths and inspect recorded values and dimensions.
Insufficient evidence: Payloads, keys, order IDs or exception messages in dimensions, or one success count hiding dropped records.

Rule: Use latency, lag, age or freshness signals only when the app can measure them meaningfully. Identify the owner of unavailable broker/platform signals.
Example: Native client lag samples can measure app-visible lag; they do not prove total broker backlog, topic availability or event freshness.
Evidence: Trace each measurement to its source and explain unavailable platform-owned signals in the report.
Insufficient evidence: Placeholder gauges or unsupported freshness/availability claims.

Rule: Use the agent-owned global API boundary for custom application signals. Preserve the existing provider and Guice ownership.
Example: An app metric uses the agent global Meter without installing another SDK.
Evidence: Inspect initialization, providers, per-record instrumentation and Guice bindings.
Insufficient evidence: OpenTelemetrySdk construction, duplicate providers, broad manual spans for each record, or a Guice Tracer binding.

Rule: Add focused tests for valid records, null/malformed records and the custom telemetry paths. Run the existing Maven tests or document the concrete blocker.
Example: The same parser test proves its business result and the expected handled-drop metric.
Evidence: Show exact commands, test results and exercised paths; identify missing dependencies or runtime prerequisites precisely.
Insufficient evidence: Compilation alone for changed parser behavior, unrun tests described as passing, or a vague environment excuse.

Rule: Explain which exact signals shorten detection time and which only help locate an incident. Keep unimplemented work and dependencies explicit.
Example: A handled-drop rate can detect silent loss; a trace may only identify the failing stage.
Evidence: Match .observe reports to implemented signals, test/runtime evidence and outstanding broker/dependency prerequisites.
Insufficient evidence: A generic MTTD claim, or local tests presented as proof of unrun broker or agent delivery.
